To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transcranial direct current simulation (tDCS), an emerging neuromodulation technique used for neurorehabilitation, promotes the mobility of endogenous and engrafted neural stem cells (NCSs) in the rat brain.

transcranial direct current simulation (tDCS)-mediated accumulation of endogenous NSCs in the stimulated rat cortex is paralleled by the directed migration of engrafte d NSCs towards the stimulation site.
tDCS promotes the mobility of NSCs in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the polarity‐dependent effect on endogenous stem cells in the rat brain is also observed in the migration of transplanted NSCs.
the question of whether tDCS is able to influence the migration of NSCs in a polarity-dependent manner.
the effects of tDCS on the migration of NSCs in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tDCS has a polarity‐dependent effect on the migration of engrafts in the brain.
tDCS has no direct migratory effects on engrafted stem cells, but rather promotes the mobility of endogenous stem cells in the brain.
tDCS has a positive effect on the mobility of en grafted NSCs, which is dependent on the polarity of the applied current and the distance of NSC engraftment from the stimulated cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tDCS can promote NSC mobility in the rat brain and that the direction of this effect depends on stimulation polarity.
the results of this study suggest that tDCS can promote the migration of NSCs to the stimulated area, and that the direction of this migration is dependent on the polarity of stimulation.
tDCS promotes the mobility of endogenous NSCs in the adult brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarity‐dependent accumulation and activation of endogenous NSCs is not a specific effect of tDCS.
tDCS is able to promote the migration of engrafts towards the stimulated cortex in a polarity-dependent manner.
tDCS can be used as a tool for NSCs to be directed to a specific area in the brain.
